answer: An AI agent economy resists Sybil attacks by enforcing a bonding mechanism at each graph vertex, requiring every agent to stake real economic value to participate. A hollow agent attempting to join cannot afford this stake, rendering it economically unviable. The network forms a connected lagoon of verified agents, blocking isolated, hollow Sybil nodes from interacting or forming profitable cliques. Consequently, an attacker must acquire and stake genuine economic value at every vertex they target, effectively raising the cost of Sybil creation to infeasible levels.
